slots.title: Jobless claims, Q3 productivity due 8:30
slots.body:
At 8:30 a.m.
ET today (Nov. 5, 2026), the U.S. calendar includes high-impact labor prints.

Initial jobless claims (week ended Oct. 31): consensus 196K vs prior 194K.

Jobless claims 4-week average: consensus 196K vs prior 196.75K.

Continuing jobless claims (Oct. 24): consensus 1,710K vs prior 1,701K.

Nonfarm productivity (Q3, quarter-over-quarter): consensus +2.8% vs prior +1.4% — output per hour in the economy, not a jobs count.

No actual results were in the morning data feed ahead of the release window.

Tomorrow’s calendar adds October payrolls and the unemployment rate at the same time.

Which print do you watch first — weekly claims or productivity?

slots.title: US cash session recap — Nov. 5, 2026
slots.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed +3.0% (+1,569.40 points) at 53,356.12, the largest percentage gain among the major U.S. benchmarks in the injected close data.

The S&P 500 finished +1.6% at 7,688.62 and the Nasdaq Composite +1.4% at 25,736.51; the Russell 2000 was +1.6% at 2,856.95.

The VIX — a gauge of expected stock-market swings — fell 20.3% to 16.61, from a prior close of 20.83.

Coverage after the midterm elections described a broad “relief” tone in equities, with lower oil prices cited alongside the move in stocks.

Gold futures rose 1.9% to 4,150.60; the U.S. dollar proxy ($UUP) was -0.4% at 28.90 and bitcoin was roughly flat at 80,354.50 (-0.1%).

Oil-related instruments were weak:
- $USO -8.1%
- $XOM -4.5%
- $COP -5.2%
- $EOG -5.2%

Apple ($AAPL) led megacap attention at +5.3% to 349.51, with a session high of 354.47 matching its 52-week high in the dataset.

Semiconductor and AI-linked heavyweights were softer despite the index rally:
- $NVDA -3.2% to 200.13
- $AVGO -2.0% to 325.48
- $SOXL -8.8% to 66.68

Alphabet ($GOOGL) rose 3.2% to 288.93; payment networks and banks participated in the up tape:
- $V +3.8% to 436.57
- $MA +3.9% to 672.68
- $BAC +4.0% to 51.63

Airbnb ($ABNB) closed +5.6% to 176.37 ahead of its scheduled earnings date; Alibaba ($BABA) was +4.9% to 105.32.

Kimberly-Clark ($KMB) reported EPS of 1.70 vs 1.65 estimated and revenue of 4.13B vs 4.13B estimated, with the stock +4.1% at 108.79.

Northwestern Energy ($NWE) posted EPS of 0.58 vs 0.733 estimated and revenue of 423.8M vs 412.3M estimated, and still finished +2.6% at 82.00.

The economic calendar listed U.S. jobless claims and nonfarm productivity for 2026-11-05 at 13:30 ET; the injected bundle did not include released actuals for those prints.

Treasury yields in the file were dated 2026-11-03, with the 10-year at 5.0% and the 2s10s spread at 0.34 percentage points.

Overseas indexes in the snapshot were mixed versus the U.S. close: Hang Seng +2.9%, FTSE +1.8%, Germany ETF proxy +3.4%, and Nikkei -1.5%.
